newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan banks seen making Eurotunnel provisions.
newsitem.headline: More Japan banks seen making Eurotunnel provisions.

text.p: More Japanese banks are likely to set aside provisions against their outstanding loans to Eurotunnel SA/Plc in their interim book closings at the end of September, bankers said on Friday.
About 1.63 billion stg worth of Eurotunnel's eight billion stg worth of junior-ranked debt is held by a group of 36 Japanese banks, bankers said.
Some Japanese banks have already made provisions of up to 50 percent against their loan exposure to the troubled Anglo-French channel tunnel operator by the annual book closing at the end of March.

Eurotunnel said earlier this month it still hoped to reach a debt restructuring agreement with its 220-bank syndicate by the end of September. But it said it had yet to resolve the key question of how much of a burden should be borne by shareholders or by bank lenders.
"Provisioning against Eurotunnel is not tax deductable, so banks need to prioritise which bad assets should be provisioned first," a banker here said.
The Eurotunnel debt has put an additional strain on Japanese commercial banks, which are already suffering from exposure to the bad loans of debt laden mortgage companies.
Eurotunnel has been in talks with banks since it froze payments on its junior-ranked loans a year ago after it undershot cash targets in 1995.
A mandate for two mediators named by a Paris court to help negotiations expires at the end of September.
